title: Self-Distilling Generative Adversarial Networks
claim: Augmenting standard adversarial training with a loss from a slowly averaged copy of the model supplies extra guidance at no added cost.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right flow, orange branch for added loss, dotted gradient paths
description: A block diagram of a GAN training loop. At the top left, a cylinder labeled Real Data sends X by a long arrow to a gray trapezoid discriminator D on the right, which outputs Real/Fake. Below, a latent vector Z drawn as a stacked column feeds two trapezoids: the generator G and the EMA generator G_EMA. A hollow arrow labeled EMA runs from G down to G_EMA. G sends generated samples X' to D. Dotted arrows show gradients flowing back from D to G. The added self-distillation path is in orange. Outputs from G and G_EMA go into an orange box labeled Perceptual Loss, and a dotted orange gradient returns only to G. The orange box and arrows draw the eye first against the gray standard GAN components.
caption: Overview of the \mname framework. The training is guided by both the conventional GAN loss and the self-distillation loss. Dotted lines indicate gradient flow; gradients from the perceptual loss do not propagate through \Gema.
abstract: In modern GANs, maintaining an Exponential Moving Average (EMA) of the generator's weights is a standard practice, as such an averaged model consistently outperforms the actively trained generator. However, the EMA generator is used for final deployment only and does not influence the training process. To address this missed opportunity, we introduce Self-Distilled GAN (SD-GAN) that employs the EMA generator as a teacher to guide the active generator (student) via perceptual loss. We prove the local asymptotic stability of SD-GAN in the simplified continuous-time Dirac-GAN setting and show that it dampens the parasitic cycling behavior that plagues conventional GANs. Empirical evaluations across established architectures and datasets demonstrate that SD-GAN improves the final image quality on several metrics (FID and random-FID in particular), stabilizes the optimization trajectory and provides additional learning guidance that is not trivially correlated with the conventional adversarial loss. It also proves effective for fine-tuning pretrained GAN models.
